# 1812: The Whole Story

> A citation-rich public-history site about the War of 1812, combining a nineteen-chapter narrative with maps, timelines, evidence panels, source packets, objects, people, places, ships, and interactive historical systems.

Website: https://war1812.jameshoward.us/
Creator: James P. Howard, II

## Start here

- [Story](https://war1812.jameshoward.us/story/): the full nineteen-chapter narrative.
- [The war in five minutes](https://war1812.jameshoward.us/five-minutes/): very short orientation.
- [The war in twenty minutes](https://war1812.jameshoward.us/twenty-minutes/): compact narrative overview.
- [Explore](https://war1812.jameshoward.us/explore/): entry point to the site's reference and interpretive layers.

## Evidence and reference

- [Timeline](https://war1812.jameshoward.us/timeline/): chronological orientation.
- [Map](https://war1812.jameshoward.us/map/): geographic exploration.
- [Evidence](https://war1812.jameshoward.us/evidence/): claim-level evidence and uncertainty.
- [Documents](https://war1812.jameshoward.us/documents/): documentary and primary-source material.
- [Sources](https://war1812.jameshoward.us/sources/): source collections and citation paths.
- [People](https://war1812.jameshoward.us/people/): people connected to the conflict.
- [Places](https://war1812.jameshoward.us/places/): locations and geographic context.
- [Ships](https://war1812.jameshoward.us/ships/): naval records and context.
- [Objects](https://war1812.jameshoward.us/objects/): material-culture records.
- [1812 Today](https://war1812.jameshoward.us/news/): current news, discoveries, and scholarship connected to the war.

## Interpretation notes

The project distinguishes documented fact from inference, later memory, oral or community tradition, dispute, and uncertainty. Prefer the evidence and source layers when evaluating a contested claim; do not flatten qualified statements into certainty.

- [James Howard](https://jameshoward.us/): creator profile and related scholarship.
